evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Not asked. Rep jumps directly to pricing without exploring customer concerns.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by the customer because the two-concerns question was never asked.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Never addressed. Rep offered Friday/Saturday packing-move split but did not identify the day's value tier or offer a cheaper alternative day with dollar savings.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Rate lock mentioned: 'we do not require any deposit nor do we have any rescheduling fees'. But the ask for the business was never explicitly given — rep said 'whenever you're ready to get it scheduled let us know' and customer responded 'I'll do that. Okay let me give you a callback once I designed,' ending in 'Sounds no problem. I'll send everything over in an email.' Rep accepted a callback instead of closing on the call.

top_strength: Jules delivered detailed pricing transparency, breaking down hourly rates ($103/hr), material costs ($250–$350 for boxes), trip fees ($115), and crew sizes (2 for packing, 4+2 trucks for moving), with clear itemization of what is and is not included.
coaching_note: Open with the customer's name and use it; ask the two-concerns question before pricing; deliver the two promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) early to build trust; and close with an explicit, unsoftened ask for the business rather than accepting a callback.
